text: Closed to vehicles at the Eldorado gate near mile 20 for maintenance as of late October 2026, with no reopening date; walkers and bikes can pass, which adds about 3 miles each way to the Cascade Pass trailhead.

SR-20 is paved and generally in good condition but closes seasonally over Washington Pass/Rainy Pass (typically mid-November through April/May depending on snowpack). Silver-Skagit Road is a rough ~39-mile gravel road from Hope, BC, but provides no legal access to Castle Peak: the Hozomeen border gate has been closed to crossing since 2020, with no end date given on the park's fire-closure page updated 14 September 2026, and the road itself has been closed at km 6 for wildfire since 24 July 2026.

Paved the full 34 miles from Granite Falls to Barlow Pass Trailhead. Beyond the trailhead, the Monte Cristo Road is gravel, gated, and closed to motor vehicles — hike or bike the 4 miles to the townsite. Alternate approach to Blanca Lake: from Index, take Index-Galena Road/FR 63 roughly 13.8 miles paved plus 2 miles gravel to the Blanca Lake Trailhead. That road has been closed to vehicles between mileposts 10 and 14 since December 2025 flood damage, with no repair timeline, and the Beckler Road/Jack Pass detour is closed too (Forest Service alert of June 30, 2026), so the Blanca Lake Trailhead cannot be reached by car; check with the Skykomish Ranger District, (360) 677-2414, before you go.

The whole Stetattle Creek Trail is under a long-term post-fire hazard closure (falling dead trees and other ground hazards), in place until further notice; check its status with North Cascades National Park before a trip.

The Labor Mountain Fire closure order (06-17-03-2026-14) on the Beverly Turnpike and Bean Creek trails has been lifted, as the Cle Elum Ranger District's trail crew reported on September 25, 2026. Beverly Turnpike has been logged out to the Fourth Creek junction, but the Bean Creek Trail still has trees down and is overgrown in places, and both trails run through burned forest where dead trees can fall and many campsites, including those in Bean Basin, burned. FR 9737-112 remains closed to vehicles after a washout, so the approach begins with a mile-plus road walk. Beyond that, Teanaway roads are snow-gated in winter/spring.

Closed to vehicles at the Eldorado gate near mile 20 for maintenance as of late October 2026, with no reopening date; walkers and bikes can pass, which adds about 3 miles each way to the Cascade Pass trailhead.

The B.C. side is shut each winter, roughly mid-October to mid-April. The NPS gate at the international boundary at Hozomeen has separately been closed to both vehicles and foot traffic since 2020, until further notice.

The NPS gate at the international border at Hozomeen has been closed to vehicle and foot traffic since 2020, until further notice. The Border 2 Fire closed the entire Hozomeen area, including both campground loops, the docks, the Obelisk Trail and the Hozomeen Cross-country Zone, and closed Silver-Skagit Road at the km 6 gate on the B.C. side. Check the park's fire-closure page and B.C. road advisories before planning.

The NPS gate at the international boundary at Hozomeen has been closed to both vehicle and foot traffic since 2020, and the park's fire-closure page, updated 14 September 2026, still lists it closed with no end date given — crossing there is prohibited and you must use a staffed port of entry. The Silver-Skagit Road has been closed to the public at the km 6 gate since 24 July 2026, when BC Parks closed Skagit Valley Provincial Park for wildfire; the B.C. Ministry of Transportation and Transit advisory, last updated 8 September 2026, gives no end date and keeps the road closed while the park is. On the US side, the park has also closed the entire Hozomeen area and the Hozomeen Cross-country Zone for the Border 2 Fire, with no end date given on the same 14 September 2026 page. Verify all three before committing to a trip.

B.C. closes Silver-Skagit Road for a seasonal winter shutdown, posted for 15 October 2025 to 14 April 2026. Separately and more importantly, the NPS gate at the international boundary at Hozomeen has been closed since 2020, with vehicle and foot traffic across the border there prohibited and no end date given on the park's fire-closure page updated 14 September 2026; the crossing has never been staffed and is camera-monitored.

Ministry of Transportation and Transit advisory, last updated 8 September 2026, gives no end date and keeps the road closed while the park is. The park has also closed the entire Hozomeen area and the Hozomeen Cross-country Zone for the Border 2 Fire, with no end date given on the same 14 September 2026 page. Confirm all three with NPS and DriveBC before committing to the trip.

SR-20 is open seasonally and closes for winter avalanche danger (recent closures have run roughly early December through spring) between the Ross Dam trailhead and Silver Star Gate — check WSDOT/NPS road conditions before driving. The Silver Skagit Road has been closed at km 6 for wildfire since 24 July 2026, with no end date given in the B.C. Ministry of Transportation and Transit closure notice last updated 24 September 2026, and the border crossing into Hozomeen has been closed to travelers since 2020.

Closed to vehicles at the Eldorado gate near mile 20 for maintenance as of late October 2026, with no reopening date; walkers and bikes can pass, which adds about 3 miles each way to the Cascade Pass trailhead.

Brush Creek Trail (the final approach corridor toward Whatcom Pass/Indian Mountain) reopened Sept. 2025 after a 3-year closure from the 2022 Brush Creek Fire; Graybeal, Graybeal Stock, and Whatcom Camps remain closed until further notice, with no end date given, as listed on the North Cascades National Park fire-closures page updated September 14, 2026, and the trail is not fully stock-accessible. The Chilliwack River Trail has been cleared of down trees as far as Bear Creek Camp, as listed on the park's trail report of September 3, 2026, but is still brushy north of the Copper Ridge junction. Bear Creek Camp is closed from 2021 fire damage, as still listed on the park's trail-conditions page updated September 17, 2026. A bypass has been built around a prior washout at the end of FR 32 to keep the Hannegan Trailhead reachable — check Mt. Baker Ranger District alerts before driving.

Decent gravel for roughly the first 11 miles from WA-207, then narrow, rough, and high-clearance-recommended for the final ~12 miles to Trinity Trailhead; sections beyond Goose Creek have been closed in some years by flood damage and wildfire activity. Storm damage has closed the road to vehicles beyond the Atkinson Flat Campground junction, with no reopening estimate, cutting off the Trinity and Phelps Creek trailheads, and a wildfire closure has also covered the Chiwawa River Road and Phelps Creek Road. Check with the Wenatchee River Ranger District, (509) 548-2550, before you go.

North Cascades NP fire closures, page last updated 14 September 2026: the Border 2 Fire closure is still in effect, but neither Ross Lake north of Lightning Creek nor the Silver Creek boat-in camp is closed by it any longer - both were on the August list and neither appears on the current one. Still closed: the entire Hozomeen area and the Hozomeen Cross-country Zone; the Willow Lake, Hozomeen Lake, Obelisk and Desolation Lookout trails; Lightning Creek from the Willow Lake Trail to Deerlick Camp; and the Boundary Bay, Nightmare, Willow Lake, Hozomeen Lake, Desolation and Deerlick camps. Depot Creek is not on the closure list. This is a dated snapshot - re-read the park's fire-closure page before relying on it.

Hannegan Pass Road (FR 32) has had storm-damage sections in recent years limiting vehicle access near the trailhead — verify current status with the Mt. Baker Ranger District/Glacier Public Service Center before driving out. Whatcom Camp, the trail camp just below Whatcom Pass, and Graybeal Camp on Brush Creek are closed until further notice because of fire-damaged hazard trees.
Sibley Creek Road 1540 has been closed by a washout since early July 2026 with no end date given, so about 2 miles of the road are walked to reach the Hidden Lake trailhead.

FSR 1540 (Sibley Creek/Hidden Lake Road) has been closed since July 8, 2026 due to a washout around mile 2.6 — confirm current status with the Mt. Baker Ranger District, (360) 854-2553, before attempting this route.

From Enumclaw, drive SR 410 east about 43 miles to the White River entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, turn right onto Sunrise Road and go about 5 miles, cross the White River, then turn left onto White River Road and follow it to its end at White River Campground. The Mowich Lake and Carbon River approaches to the northwest side have been closed at the SR 165 bridge since April 2025.

No closure is currently posted for FS 31 (Canyon Creek Road) or the FS 3160 spur, but the road has a history of slide and washout damage. Verify current status with the Glacier Public Service Center or MBS road-conditions page before the trip.

Drive to Chelan or Field's Point Landing, take the Lady of the Lake ferry (~4 hr) to Lucerne, then a Forest Service/Holden Village bus (~11 miles) to Holden Village and the Holden Campground trailhead. No drivable road reaches the peak. Note: as of the Dec 2025 flood/landslide, FR 8301 and Holden Village are closed under USFS order #06-17-05-26-04, in effect 28 January 2026 through 31 December 2027 — this normal approach is not currently usable; check Chelan Ranger District status before relying on it.

Drive to Chelan/Field's Point, then take the Lady of the Lake boat to Lucerne; shuttle to Holden Village and hike in via the same approach as the Mary Green Glacier route. No drivable road to the trailhead. Note: as of the Dec 2025 flood/landslide, FR 8301 and Holden Village are closed under USFS order #06-17-05-26-04, in effect 28 January 2026 through 31 December 2027, so this normal ferry/shuttle approach is not currently usable — check Chelan Ranger District status before relying on it.
Private road access via Alpental Community Club roads restricted as of 2021; use established alternatives
Alpental Community Club private roads ('...Strasse' names) above the ski area are off-limits to public foot and vehicle access as of 2021 - use the Snow Lake trailhead boot path approach instead.

The Olney Creek Road gate location has moved over the years — near mile 10-11 from the highway as of 2009, but in the 2020s parties describe it closed much closer to the Sultan Basin Road junction. Treat any specific older driving mileage as unreliable and check current conditions first.

Roads cross private industrial timberland whose ownership has changed hands over the years (currently Hampton Family Forests, which requires a paid recreation permit); gate locations, mileage, and any permission requirements can change without notice — verify current status with the landowner before driving. Many parties bike the lower logging-road miles to save time.

Drive to Chelan or Field's Point Landing, take the Lady of the Lake ferry (~4 hr) to Lucerne, then a Forest Service/Holden Village bus to Holden Village; hike in via the Railroad Creek Trail to Hart Lake. No drivable road reaches the peak. Note: as of the Dec 2025 flood/landslide, FR 8301 and Holden Village are closed under USFS order #06-17-05-26-04, in effect 28 January 2026 through 31 December 2027 — this normal approach is not currently usable; check Chelan Ranger District status before relying on it.

B.C. winter shutdown posted 15 October 2025 to 14 April 2026. The NPS gate at the international boundary at Hozomeen has been closed to vehicle and foot traffic since 2020, with no end date given on the park's fire-closure page updated 14 September 2026.

NPS border gate at Hozomeen closed to vehicle and foot traffic since 2020; still closed, with no end date given, on the park's fire-closure page updated 14 September 2026. Silver-Skagit Road closed to the public at the km 6 gate since 24 July 2026 for wildfire; no end date given in the B.C. Ministry of Transportation and Transit advisory last updated 8 September 2026. NPS has also closed the entire Hozomeen area and the Hozomeen Cross-country Zone for the Border 2 Fire, no end date given as of that 14 September 2026 page.
